Interface OidcActor

public interface OidcActor
The act claim: who is really behind a token issued for somebody else.

Set only when an impersonation request is honored, and then on both tokens. The two carry different amounts of it: an access token names the actor and nothing more, since a resource server needs to know an action was delegated and not who the delegate is, while an ID token adds name and email so a relying party can show its user whose session they are looking through. Both are the actor's own claims, never the subject's.

A bean, so a token builder renders it as the nested object RFC 8693 defines rather than as a string. The two optional claims are omitted from the rendering when they answer null, which is what makes one interface serve both tokens.
